rationale: The same scene in the same order: a withdrawal by boat to a solitary place, crowds following on foot, the disciples saying "This is a desolate place, and the hour is already late" (Matthew 14:15; Mark 6:35, BSB), the reply "You give them something to eat" (Matthew 14:16; Mark 6:37), five loaves and two fish, Jesus "looking up to heaven" before He blessed and broke, "They all ate and were satisfied" (Matthew 14:20; Mark 6:42), and twelve basketfuls; the Greek basket word is kophinos in both. Parallel/strong rather than explicit, following conn-matt12-sabbath-mark2, because neither Gospel names the other and the differences are real and checkable in the BSB. In Mark the occasion is the apostles' return (6:30-31); in Matthew it is the news about John (14:12-13). Only Mark has "like sheep without a shepherd" and "He began to teach them many things" (6:34), "two hundred denarii" (6:37), "groups of hundreds and fifties" on "the green grass" (6:39-40), and the divided fish (6:41). Where Mark has teaching, Matthew has "healed their sick" (14:14), and only Matthew adds "in addition to women and children" (14:21).
